record.original_question: Let f(t) be a continuous T-periodic function with f not identically zero and let p>0. Find necessary and sufficient conditions on f that guarantee the singular second-order equation x(t)^p x''(t) = f(t) has positive T-periodic solutions.

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Let f(t) be a continuous T periodic function, f(t) not identically 0 and 0 < p in R. Find necessary and sufficient conditions on the function f that ensure the existence of positive T periodic solutions of x^p(t)x''(t) = f(t).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T>0$ and $p>0$ be real numbers, and let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a continuous $T$-periodic function that is not identically zero. Consider the singular second-order ordinary differential equation
$$x(t)^{p}\, x''(t) = f(t).$$
A function $x:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called a positive $T$-periodic solution if it is of class $C^{2}$, satisfies $x(t+T)=x(t)$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$, $x(t)>0$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$, and satisfies the equation pointwise.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $f$ (and possibly on $p$) under which the above equation admits at least one positive $T$-periodic solution.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a published characterization giving necessary and sufficient conditions on $f$ for the existence of positive $T$-periodic solutions of $x^p x'' = f(t)$ for general $p>0$. Related work treats sufficient conditions or different classes of singular/superlinear equations, but a complete necessary-and-sufficient criterion for this specific equation does not appear to be known.

status_evidence.title: Existence of a periodic solution for superlinear second order ODEs
status_evidence.snippet: Research proves necessary and sufficient conditions for periodic solutions of superlinear second-order ODEs under certain assumptions, but for a different equation class.
status_evidence.claim: Related results address necessary/sufficient conditions for related but distinct second-order periodic problems, not the specific singular equation x^p x'' = f(t).
